A bit surprising how much Claude struggled with these proofs of quite modest complexity (and with given step by step informal guide). In my own experiments with Real Analysis proofs, claude has been capable of proving much longer and harder results, but maybe having more instances of informal solution in training is implicitly helping (those are standard Real Analysis proofs).

Screenshot 2026-03-08 at 4.00.34 PM.png

What is the Lean hook, that claude mentions here? My setup for claude in vs code for lean work is through - https://github.com/oOo0oOo/lean-lsp-mcp and it looks like

Screenshot 2026-03-08 at 4.04.19 PM.png

I am trying to find out the best Lean <> Claude code setup in terms of speed of feedback, but it such a novel space, it is hard to make sense of all LSP, MCP, hooks, etc.
I think it would be interesting to see how large language models compare to small language models
In my experience, claude code does great on the proofs I am trying to formalize (undergraduate level math) and produces much more readable proofs than Aristotle.

It doesn't one shot things as much but given time it figures out some lean tricks. I have told it to record them in an TACTICS.md - https://github.com/rkirov/analysis/blob/main/TACTICS.md. Sometimes it ignores them when the context window gets large

@Rado Kirov You can try the Lean Skill by Cameron Freer, I heard its not bad for Agentic Lean Usage. Here is the link to the topic #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > Lean Skill for Claude Code, at the the top you can find the link to the repo / skill.
